questions.question: What is Net National Product?

options.text: The product of gross national product and depreciation is net national product.
The sum of gross national product and income of foreigners is net national product.
Net national product is equal to gross national product.
The difference between gross national product and depreciation is net national product.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The difference between gross national product and depreciation is net national product.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product is a measure of the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, minus the value of capital goods used up in the production process.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)** is the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of their location, in a specific period of time (usually a year). It includes the value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens and businesses, both domestically and abroad.
 
• ** Depreciation refers to the decrease in the value of capital goods (**such as machinery, buildings, and vehicles) over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, and other factors. It is subtracted from GNP to arrive at Shuddh Rashtriya Utpad, which provides a more accurate measure of a country's economic output.
 
• ** Shuddh Rashtriya Utpad is also known as Net National Product (NNP)** and represents the income earned by a country's residents from the production of goods and services. It is a key measure of a country's economic performance and is used to calculate other indicators such as per capita income and the Human Development Index.

questions.question: If there is a fall in the demand of a good, the equilibrium price is expected to:

options.text: first rise, and then fall sharply

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fall**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When there is a fall in the demand for a good, the equilibrium price is expected to **fall**.
 
• The equilibrium price is determined by the intersection of the demand and supply curves. A decrease in demand shifts the demand curve to the left.
 
• This shift results in a new equilibrium where the quantity demanded and supplied are lower, leading to a lower price.
 
• Other factors being constant, a fall in demand reduces the competition for the good, causing sellers to lower prices to attract buyers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The equilibrium price is the price at which the quantity of a good demanded by consumers equals the quantity supplied by producers.
 
• A shift in the demand or supply curve can lead to a new equilibrium price and quantity.
 
• Factors that can cause a fall in demand include a decrease in consumer income, changes in tastes and preferences, and the availability of substitutes.
 
• Understanding the dynamics of demand and supply is crucial for predicting market behavior and making informed economic decisions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the methods of national income estimation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banking method**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• National income is the total value of a country’s final output of all new goods and services produced in one year.
 
• Methods of measuring national income are:

 
• Expenditure Method - Under this method, we estimate the disposal of income on the purchase of final goods and services.
 
• Income Method - The Income Method measures national income from the side of payments made to the primary factors of production in the form of rent, wages, interest, and profit for their productive services in an accounting year. 
 
• Production method - In this method, national income is measured as a flow of goods and services. This method is also called an **output method**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• 
 Measurement of National Income

 
 
• 
 There are three methods to measure national income:

 
 
• **Income Method**
 
• **Production (Value-Added) Method**
 
• **Expenditure Method**
 
 
 
• 
 Measurement of National Income – Income Method

 
 
• Estimated by adding all the factors of production (rent, wages, interest, profit) and the mixed-income of self-employed.
 
• In India, one-third of people are self-employed
 
• This is the ‘**domestic**’ income, related to the production within the borders of the country
 
 
 
• Measurement of National Income – Production Method
 
 
• Estimated by adding the value added by all the firms.
 
• **Value-added** = Value of Output – Value of (non-factor) inputs
 

 
 
• This gives** GDP at Market Price (MP) – because it includes depreciation (therefore ‘gross’) and taxes (thus ‘market price’)**
 
• To reach National Income (that is, NNP at FC)
 

 
 
• Add Net Factor Income from Abroad: **GNP at MP = GDP at MP + NFIA**
 
• Subtract Depreciation:** NNP at MP = GNP at MP – Dep**
 
• Subtract Net Indirect Taxes: **NNP at FC = NNP at MP – NIT**
 
 
 
• Measurement of National Income – Expenditure Method
 
 
• The expenditure method to measure national income can be understood by the equation given below: 
 
 
• **Y = C + I + G + (X-M),**
 
• where** Y = GDP at MP, C = Private Sector’s Expenditure on final consumer goods, G = Govt’s expenditure on final consumer goods, I = Investment or Capital Formation, X = Exports, X- M = Net Exports (difference between exports (X) and imports (M))**
 
 
 
 
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• GDP: Gross Domestic Product is the sum of the money of all the final goods and services produced solely within the boundaries of a country, at a specific time.

 
 
• GDP includes the income of foreigners staying in the country.
 
• It excludes the income of nationals of the country staying abroad and also excludes the remittances sent from abroad.
 
 
 
• GNP: Gross National Product is the sum of the money of all the final goods and services produced both within and outside of a country by nationals during a specific period of time.
 
 
• GNP includes remittances.
 
• It excludes income generated locally by non-nationals.

questions.question: If GNP is 16% higher than the last year and the rate of inflation is 9%, production in the economy has grown by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.07**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gross National Product (GNP) is a broad measure of a nation's total economic activity.
 
• The GNP is 16% higher than the last year, indicating overall economic growth.
 
• Inflation rate is 9%, which represents the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services is rising.
 
• The production growth rate can be determined by adjusting the GNP growth rate for inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)**

 
 
• GNP measures the market value of all the products and services produced in one year by labor and property supplied by the residents of a country.
 
• It includes the value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of the location of the actual production.
 
 
 
• **Inflation**
 
 
• Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services is rising and subsequently eroding purchasing power.
 
• Central banks attempt to limit inflation, and avoid deflation, in order to keep the economy running smoothly.
 
 
 
• **Economic Growth**
 
 
• Economic growth is an increase in the production of economic goods and services, compared from one period of time to another.
 
• It can be measured in nominal or real terms, the latter of which is adjusted for inflation.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Production Growth Rate**
 
 
• To find the production growth rate, we adjust the GNP growth rate for inflation.
 
• Formula: Production Growth Rate = (1 + GNP Growth Rate) / (1 + Inflation Rate) - 1
 
• Using the given values: GNP Growth Rate = 16% or 0.16, Inflation Rate = 9% or 0.09
 
• Production Growth Rate = (1 + 0.16) / (1 + 0.09) - 1 = 1.16 / 1.09 - 1 = 1.0642 - 1 ≈ 0.07

questions.question: When a person seems to be working, but their work is not contributing to the output, it is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disguised unemployment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a person seems to be working, but their work is not contributing to the output, it is known as disguised unemployment. 
 
• Disguised unemployment is a type of unemployment where people are employed but their contribution to the total output is negligible.
 
• Even if some workers are removed, the output of the task remains unaffected.
 
• This often happens in agricultural sectors where family members work on a small plot of land, even though their contribution to the output is minimal.
 
• It's also known as hidden unemployment

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cyclical Unemployment:
 
 
• Occurs due to fluctuations in the business cycle.
 
• During economic downturns, businesses reduce production and lay off workers, leading to a rise in unemployment.
 
• As the economy recovers, employment levels rise again.
 
 
 
• Frictional Unemployment:
 
 
• Occurs when people are temporarily unemployed while transitioning between jobs.
 
• This can happen for various reasons, such as quitting a job voluntarily, getting layoffs, or searching for a job after completing education.
 
• It's considered a normal part of a healthy economy as people move between jobs to find better opportunities.
 
 
 
• Seasonal Unemployment:
 
 
• Occurs due to seasonal variations in demand for labor.
 
• Certain industries, like tourism, agriculture, and construction, experience fluctuations in demand throughout the year.
 
• As a result, workers in these industries may be unemployed during off-peak seasons.

questions.question: What is net investment?

options.text: Sum of all the investments in a country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross investment - depreciation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A company's net investment is the sum of its expenditures on capital assets less the cost of depreciating those assets.
 
• This gives an idea of the actual spending on durable products utilized by the company in its operations, such as buildings, machinery, and software.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Depreciation: It means a fall in the value of an asset because of usage or with efflux of time or due to obsolescence or accident.
 
• Appreciation: It means an increase in the value of an asset over time. This the opposite of depreciation. It is an upward adjustment of the value of an asset held on a company's accounting book.
 
• Deceleration: It is the rate at which an asset's value in the market goes down.
 
• Gross investment: It is the total amount spent on goods in order to produce other goods and services. 
 
• Net investment: It is the amount of increase in productive stock.
 
• 
 
Capital investment is the money used by a business to purchase fixed assets, such as land, machinery, or buildings. The money may be in the form of cash, assets, or loans. Without capital investment, businesses may have a hard time getting off the ground.

questions.question: In national income accounting, GVA stands for ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross Value added**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross Value Added (GVA) **is a measure in **economics** used to gauge the total productivity and economic output of a region, country or specific sector of the economy.
 
• It calculates **the value of goods and services** produced in an area, industry or sector of an economy.
 
• GVA is a measure of the **value of goods and services produced in an area, industry or sector of an economy.**
 
• It is used in the production approach to** calculating GDP (Gross Domestic Product), with the formula**:
 
• **GDP = GVA + (Taxes on Products - Subsidies on Products)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In accordance with the formula,** the GDP and GVA **are connected via the net taxes (which is taxes on products minus subsidies).
 
• Put simply, **GVA** is the total value of the **goods and services a sector**,** industry or region produces**, but it doesn't account for the costs of goods and raw materials that were consumed in production.
 
• Therefore, it can be considered a measure of the gross contribution to the economy of each individual producer, industry or sector.

questions.question:
Which of the following are included in 'revenue receipts'?

(a) Tax Revenue

(b) Non-tax Revenue
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (a) and (b).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue receipts **are defined as those receipts that** neither increase a government's liabilities nor decrease its assets.**
 
• They are** routine and ongoing **in nature, and the government receives them as part of daily operations.
 
• **Taxes and other levies **collected by the Centre, **interest and dividends** received on investments, and fees and charges paid to the government for services are all considered **revenue receipts.**
 
• The **government's assets** **do not decrease **as a result of revenue collections.
 
• As a result, the government is unable to report the proceeds from the sale of a stake in a **public-sector business** as revenue because the sale of the holding reduced its assets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tax revenues and non-tax revenues** are the** two main sources** of income for the government.
 
• **Tax revenue:**
 
 
• It is the **total amount received** from all taxes and other** government-imposed levies.**
 
• Taxes are mandatory payments that **individuals and businesses** must make to the government without **expecting a direct benefit** in return.
 
 
 
• **Non Tax Revenues:**
 
 
• **Government receipts** from** all sources** other than tax receipts are referred to as non-tax revenue.
 
• **Interest, profits and dividends, fees, license fees, fines and penalties, gifts and grants, forfeitures, and special assessments **are the primary non-tax revenue streams.

questions.question: The value of final goods and services produced in a country is known as _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**national income**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

__Key Points__

__
 
• The **value of final goods and services produced in a country is known as National income.**
 
• National income** refers to the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced w**ithin a country's borders during a specific period, typically a year.
 
• It **serves as a comprehensive measure of a country's economic performance and standard of living.**
 
• National income is often calculated using various methods such as the **Production Method**, **Income Method**, and **Expenditure Method**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

Additional Information__

 
• **Components**

 
 
• **​Production Method**

 
 
• This method calculates GDP by summing the value-added at each stage of production in various sectors.
 
• Value-added refers to the difference between the value of output and the cost of intermediate goods used in production.
 
 
 
• **Income Method**
 
 
• This method calculates GDP by summing all incomes earned by individuals, businesses, and the government within a country.
 
• It Includes wages, rent, interest, and profits. Additionally, it takes into account indirect taxes and subtracts subsidies.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Expenditure Method**
 
 
• **This method calculates GDP by summing all expenditures on final goods and services in the economy.**
 
• **It Includes consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports (exports minus imports).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: According to Malthusian theory which of the following grows in geometric progression?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Population**__.

__
 
• **According to Malthusian theory, the population grows in geometric progression**__.

 __
 
• The **Malthusian Theory of Population** is the theory of exponential **population** and **arithmetic food supply growth.**
 
• The theory was proposed by **Thomas Robert Malthus**. He believed that a balance between population growth and food supply can be established through preventive and positive checks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Malthusian Theory of Population Growth:**

 
 
• Among the most famous theories of demography is the one associated with the English political economist Thomas Robert Malthus (1766-1834).
 
• Malthus's theory of population growth - outlined in his Essay on Population (1798) - was a rather pessimistic one.
 
• He argued that human populations tend to grow at a much faster rate than the rate at which the means of human subsistence (especially food, but also clothing and other agriculture-based products) can grow. Therefore humanity is condemned to live in poverty forever because the growth of agricultural production will always be overtaken by population growth.
 
• While population rises in **geometric progression** (i.e., like 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 etc.), agricultural production can only grow in arithmetic progression (i.e., like 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 etc.).
 
• Because population growth always outstrips growth in the production of subsistence resources, the only way to increase prosperity is by controlling the growth of the population.
 
• Unfortunately, humanity has only a limited ability to voluntarily reduce the growth of its population (through 'preventive checks' such as postponing marriage or practicing sexual abstinence or celibacy).
 
• Malthus believed therefore that positive checks' to population growth - in the form of famines and diseases - were inevitable because they were nature's way of dealing with the imbalance between food supply and increasing population.

__
 
• **Gross National Product (GNP) **measures the total value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents within a specific time period, including income earned by residents from investments abroad.
 
• Depreciation accounts for the reduction in value of capital goods over time due to wear and tear or obsolescence.
 
• By subtracting **depreciation from GNP, you arrive at Net National Product (NNP),** which reflects the actual value of goods and services produced, taking into account the loss of value in capital assets.
 
• The formula can be summarized as:** NNP=GNP−Depreciation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Subsidies are government financial assistance provided to individuals or businesses to **promote economic activity **and** reduce costs**.
 
• They include direct cash payments, tax breaks, price supports, and grants.
 
• Subsidies can stimulate growth and lower consumer prices but may also cause market distortions and strain government budgets.
 
• Common examples include** agricultural subsidies, energy subsidies for renewables**, and education subsidies for higher education.
 
 
 
• **Indirect taxes**
 
 
• Indirect taxes are taxes levied on goods and services rather than on income or profits, meaning they are **not directly paid by the individual but are passed on through the price of goods.**
 
• Common forms of indirect taxes include sales tax,** value-added tax (VAT),** excise duty, and customs duty.
 
• Indirect taxes increase the cost of goods and services, which can lead to higher prices for consumers, making them less visible than direct taxes.
 
• Indirect taxes are a significant **source of revenue for governments**, as they are easier to collect and can be applied to a wide range of products and services.
 
 
 
• **Personal income**
 
 
• Personal income refers to the **total earnings received by an individual from various sources,** including wages, salaries, investments, rental income, and government benefits.
 
• It includes wages, bonuses, interest income, dividends, rents, and any other forms of **earnings before taxes are deducted.**
 
• Personal income is a **key indicator of an individual's economic** health and purchasing power, influencing consumption, savings, and overall economic activity.
 
• Personal income is subject to income tax, which varies based on the individual's income level and applicable tax laws in their country or region.

questions.question: Which of the following best represents the concept of Net Domestic Product (NDP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GDP - Depreciation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net domestic product (NDP)** is an annual measure of the **economic output of a nation that is adjusted as per the depreciation effect.**
 
• The** NDP** is calculated by **subtracting depreciation from the gross domestic product (GDP).**
 
• An **increased NDP indicates growth in economic health**, while a **decrease would indicate a slowdown of the economy of the country.**
 
• **Depreciation** is the** measure of the decreased monetary value of an asset** over time due to **use, wear and tear, or obsolescence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **__Gross National Income (GNI)__**

__
 
• **Gross National Income (GNI)** is the** total amount of money earned by a nation's people and businesses.**
 
• It is used to measure and track a nation's wealth from year to year.
 
• The number is calculated using the** nation's gross domestic product (GDP) plus the income it receives from abroad.**
 
• India GNI per capita for 2020 was $1,900.

**Net National Product (NNP)__**

 
• **Net national product (NNP) **is the monetary** value of finished goods and services** produced by a country's citizens, overseas and domestically, in a given period.
 
• It is the equivalent of the **Gross National Product (GNP), the total value of a nation's annual output, minus the depreciation.**
 
• NNP is often examined on an **annual basis** as a way to measure a nation's success.

questions.question: The intervention of the government whether to expand demand or reduce it constitutes the __________ function.

__

• **​**The government can change its spending and tax levels to stimulate or slow down the economy.

• **Monetary policy**
 
 
• ** **The government can change the interest rates that it charges banks to borrow money.
 
• This can affect the amount of money that banks lend to businesses and consumers, which can in turn affect the level of economic activity.
 
• For example, if the government wants to stimulate the economy, it might lower interest rates.
 
• This would make it cheaper for businesses to borrow money, which would encourage them to invest and hire more workers.
 
 
 
• **Stabilization: **The act of stabilizing something, such as the economy.

questions.question: Which method of calculating the national income is also known as ‘Industrial Origin Method’?

• There are **three** methods for calculating national income namely **Income Method**, **Expenditure method**, and **Value Added Method**.
 
• In this article, we will understand the **value-added** **method** for calculating national income.
 
• The value-added method is used to calculate the** national income** in different stages of production in the circular flow.
 
• It represents the contribution for each producing unit in the **production** **process**. 
 
• **Value-added** refers to the additional value to the raw material by an organization, using its production activities.
 
• It is calculated as the **difference** between the value of output and the value of intermediate goods.
 
• The **value-added method** is a widely used method for calculating national income as it avoids double counting, which is quite a serious error while estimating national income.

questions.question: When the ‘trans-boundary economic activities’ of an economy and depreciation are included into account, the aggregate measure is known as ________.

• **GNP** stands for Gross National Product.
 
• GNP includes the value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of the location of the production.
 
• It accounts for 'trans-boundary economic activities' by including the income earned by residents from overseas investments and subtracting the income earned within the domestic economy by foreign residents.
 
• Depreciation is subtracted from GNP to get Net National Product (NNP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Net National Product (NNP)** is derived by subtracting depreciation from GNP.
 
• **Per Capita Income (PCI)** is the average income earned per person in a given area in a specified year.
 
• GNP is a more comprehensive measure than GDP as it considers the income from abroad.

questions.question: Which cost is considered for calculating the national income in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Factor cost.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This refers to the cost of production factors (land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship) used to produce goods and services, excluding indirect taxes and including subsidies.
 
• National income is often calculated at factor cost** to reflect the income earned by factors of production**, giving a more accurate measure of economic performance.
 
• It reflects the income earned by factors of production and provides a** clear view of the economy's performance. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Product Cost**:

 
 
• This encompasses all costs associated with** the production of goods**, including direct materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead.
 
• While product cost can influence pricing and profit calculations, it is not directly used to calculate national income in the same way as factor cost.
 
 
 
• **Market Cost**:
 
 
• This is the price at which goods and services are sold in the market, **including taxes and excluding subsidies.**
 
• National income can be expressed in terms of market prices, but adjustments for taxes and subsidies are necessary to derive factor cost for a more accurate measure.
 
 
 
• **Sunk Cost**:
 
 
• This refers to costs that have already been incurred and **cannot be recovered.** Sunk costs should not influence future economic decisions.
 
• Sunk costs are not relevant for calculating national income, as they do not reflect current production or income generation.

questions.question: _____ is calculated by dividing the nominal GDP in a given year by the real GDP for the same year and multiplying it by 100.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GDP Deflator**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **GDP deflator **is an economic indicator that measures inflation or deflation in an economy.
 
• **It is calculated by dividing the nominal GDP by the real GDP and multiplying the result by 100.**
 
• **Nominal GDP** is the value of all goods and services produced in an economy, unadjusted for inflation.
 
• **Real GDP** is the value of goods and services produced in an economy, adjusted for inflation.
 
• **The GDP **deflator helps compare the economic output of different years by adjusting for changes in price levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disposable Income:**

 
 
• Disposable income refers to the** income remaining after deduction of taxes and other mandatory charges.**
 
• It is the amount of money available for spending and saving after all deductions.
 
• Disposable income does not directly relate to **GDP calculations or inflation adjustments.**
 
 
 
• **Real Income:**
 
 
• Real income refers to the** income of individuals or nations, adjusted for inflation.**
 
• It reflects the purchasing power of income, taking into account changes in price levels.
 
• Real income is **not a measure of inflation or deflation, but rather a measure of the true value of income in terms of goods and services.**
 
 
 
• **Per Capita Income:**
 
 
• **Per capita income is a measure of the average income earned per person in a certain area or region.**
 
• It is calculated by dividing the total income of a region by its population.
 
• Per capita income is** not directly related to inflation, deflation, or GDP calculations, but is a useful metric for comparing living standards and economic development between regions.**
